landing.title: Moss’s Club house · Anonymous letters carried by Moss
landing.description: Write a worry on a typewriter. Moss carries it to another city, and a stranger writes back. Every letter is written by a person. Free on iPhone and Android.
landing.h1:
Write a worry.
Moss delivers it.
landing.lede: Someone in another city reads it and writes back.
landing.artAlt: Moss, a garden gnome with a red pointed hat and a white beard

steps.b: One letter a day, on a typewriter. No name, no profile.
Your letter goes to another city. You get up to 3 letters a day, too.
Someone picks your letter and writes back. You can send a thank-you.

facts: People write every letter. AI only checks and translates them.
Others see your letter and an approximate city. Nothing else.
Free. Optional rewarded ads are available in the shop for ages 19 and up.
landing.safety: Report or block a letter right from the letter. If you might be in danger, don’t wait for a reply. Contact local emergency services now.

support.title: Support · Moss’s Club house
support.description: Help with Moss’s Club house: contact, letters and replies, reporting and blocking, and deleting your account.
support.lede: Questions, or something not working? Write to us.
support.contactBody: We review and handle in-app feedback once a week. Tell us your phone model, its OS version and what happened on which screen, and we can help faster. You can write in any language. Please don’t include the text of anyone else’s letter. Safety reports are handled separately.
support.subject: Moss’s Club house
support.reportBody: To report a letter or reply, open it in the app and tap Report letter. Your reason and the content as you saw it reach our operators privately, so you don’t need to copy anything. You can also tap Block this sender so you won’t exchange letters with that person again.
support.dangerBody: Moss’s Club house can’t respond to emergencies. If you or someone else might be in immediate danger, contact local emergency services or someone nearby now. Don’t wait for a letter reply.

faq.a: Yes. Sign in with Apple or Google so your letters can find their way back to you. Other people never see your name or email.

faq.q: How many letters can I write?
faq.a: One worry letter a day. Each day Moss also brings you up to three letters from other people. You can reply to all of them, one at a time. Once you choose a letter, you have 48 hours to write your reply.

faq.q: My letter came back without a reply
faq.a: Sometimes nobody picks a letter in time. When that happens, Moss brings it back to you. You can write a new letter the next day.

The person who receives it. Before delivery, an automated review checks the letter and translates it into the reader’s language. AI does not write or change what you say. If a letter needs changes before it can be sent, the app tells you.

faq.q: Can people see where I live?
faq.a: No. Moss only uses an approximate city based on your network connection, and readers see only that approximate city. The app doesn’t use your phone’s GPS.

faq.q: What does burning a letter do?
faq.a: Holding to burn a draft clears it from your phone without sending it. After a reply comes back, you can also burn the letter and its reply to remove them from your archive. This can’t be undone.

faq.q: How do I cancel a membership or get a refund?
faq.a: Cancel a subscription in the subscription settings of your App Store or Google Play account. You keep the membership until the end of the period you already paid for. Deleting the app or your account does not cancel a subscription, so cancel it in the store first. Ask the store you bought from for a refund. If you changed devices, you can restore your purchase on the membership screen in the app.

The app and letter exchange are free. You can buy a paid membership if you want one, and every letter feature works without it. After opening the free set of three boxes, you can claim one spark a day if you are 18 or younger, or choose to watch a rewarded ad if you are 19 or older. Members who are 19 or older get sparks with the same odds and no ad. On iOS, ad personalization follows your tracking permission and regional consent. On Android, personalized ads are off by default and can be enabled in Settings. When personalization is not permitted, general ads may be requested. The choice does not change the reward odds or daily limit.

deleteParagraphs: In the app, open Settings and tap Delete account. You can also request deletion using the link below or by emailing us. You do not need to reinstall the app.

For a request outside the app, we verify you using a single-use confirmation link sent to the email address registered with your account, including an Apple private relay address if you use one. Where available, you may instead reauthenticate with the same sign-in provider. We do not ask for an ID, password or letter text.

We aim to acknowledge requests within 7 days and delete the account within 7 days of verification, usually within 28 days in total. Linked private feedback is removed asynchronously. We do not consider deletion complete until that cleanup is done. See the Privacy Policy for records kept for safety.

terms.title: Terms of Use · Moss’s Club house
terms.description: The rules for using Moss’s Club house: who can use it, what letters may contain, reporting, AI review and your account.
terms.h1: Moss’s Club house Terms of Use
terms.intro: Moss’s Club house (the “app”) is made by Jongmin Lee, an independent developer at JML.Studio (“we”). By creating an account or using the app, you agree to these terms. If you don’t agree, please don’t use the app.

p: The app lets people exchange anonymous letters about their worries. You can write one letter a day. Other people may receive it and write one reply. Each day the app brings you up to three letters from other people, and you can reply to each of them, one at a time, within 48 hours of choosing it. Letters are reviewed automatically and translated so they can travel between languages.

The app is not therapy, medical, legal or crisis support. Replies come from other users, not from professionals, and we don’t check whether their advice is right for you. If you might be in danger, contact local emergency services right away.

You must be at least {age} years old to use the app. If you are under the age of majority where you live, you need permission from a parent or guardian. You may not use the app if we have restricted your account or if the law where you live forbids it.

You sign in with Apple or Google. Keep your device and sign-in secure, because you are responsible for what is sent from your account. One person, one account: don’t create accounts to get around a restriction.
Moss’s Club house works because people are kind to strangers. When you write a letter or a reply, you agree not to:
list: harass, threaten, insult or shame anyone, or encourage anyone to hurt themselves or others;
post hate speech or content that attacks people for who they are;
post sexual content, or any content that sexualizes minors;
share personal information that could identify you or anyone else, such as names, phone numbers, addresses, social media accounts or photos;
ask to meet, move the conversation elsewhere, or ask for money;
advertise, spam, or send links;
post content that is illegal, or that infringes someone else’s rights;
pretend to be someone else, or use automated means to send letters.
after: We have zero tolerance for objectionable content and abusive users. You can talk about hard feelings and painful experiences. That is what the app is for. What matters is how you treat the people reading.

p: Every letter and reply is checked before delivery by an automated review that uses AI. A letter may be delivered, returned to you to revise, held, or not delivered. The review can make mistakes, and it doesn’t guarantee that every letter you receive will be appropriate.

We may use external AI services to review letters for inappropriate content and to translate them. The Privacy Policy explains what is sent and to whom. Letters can’t be delivered without this processing, so by accepting these terms you also consent to it. For letters to your future self, their text is sent to an external AI service only when you ask for a question, a summary card or a lookback. If you do not ask, it is not sent. Your acceptance of these terms covers this too. AI does not write your letters, and summary cards and lookbacks contain only passages chosen from your letters.

You can report any letter or reply you receive, and you can block its sender. We review reports and act on objectionable content as quickly as we can, aiming for within 24 hours. We may remove content, and we may restrict or end accounts that break these terms, with or without notice. A restricted account can’t send, reply or receive new letters.

You keep ownership of what you write. You give us a worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to store, review, translate, deliver and display your letters and replies to operate the app, and to keep them as described in the Privacy Policy. Once a letter is delivered, its reader can read it, and we can’t control what a reader does with what they read.
Don’t send anything you aren’t comfortable sharing with a stranger.

sections.h: 7. Sparks, daily rewards, membership and changes
p: After opening your free set of three shop boxes, you can earn one daily reward. If you are 18 or younger, you can claim one spark for checking in, without an ad. If you are 19 or older, you can choose to finish a rewarded ad when available. On iOS, ad personalization follows the tracking permission and regional consent. On Android, personalized ads are off by default and can be enabled in Settings. When personalization is not permitted, general ads may be requested. Both have the same reward odds and daily limit. The chances are 1 spark: 2%; 2: 20%; 3: 50%; 4: 20%; 5: 8%. Both methods share one reward limit per account per day, resetting at local midnight. If you have a membership and said you are 19 or older, you get sparks with the same odds without watching the ad. The daily limit and the odds are the same as for people without a membership. The app has no way to change a saved age group; to correct it, contact us. You can use sparks to open shop boxes. Sparks and items from boxes have no cash value and cannot be purchased with real money, transferred or redeemed for cash. A membership does not give sparks, boxes or items from boxes.

Without a membership, you can send 1 letter to your future self a day for 4 sparks. If you said you are 19 or older, you can choose to watch a rewarded ad to the end and send it for 2 sparks instead. This ad is counted separately from the daily reward. With a membership, you can send 3 a day without spending sparks. Deleting a letter does not give back the sparks or that day’s letter. While writing one letter, you can ask for up to 2 questions without a membership and up to 5 with one. A summary card is one per letter that has come back, and you can make up to 3 a day without a membership and up to 10 with one. A lookback can be made for a period that has ended when at least 3 letters came back in it for My week, 8 for My month and 12 for My year. Without a membership you see part of My week, and My month and My year need a membership.
Writing, receiving and replying to letters, and the shop, are free. You can use all of them without a membership.
list: Membership. You can choose to buy a paid membership. It adds members-only looks and convenience features, and the membership screen in the app shows what is included before you buy. Some benefits may not be available on every device or operating system. A membership does not change how many worry letters, replies or encouragement letters you can send, which letters you receive, the order of delivery or your chance of getting a reply. The limits for letters to your future self, with and without a membership, are those stated above in this section.

Products and prices. Membership is sold as a monthly subscription and a yearly subscription, which both renew automatically. Prices differ by country or region, and the store’s purchase screen shows your price before you pay. A launch or introductory price, when one is offered, applies only to the first period, and the subscription then renews at the regular price shown on the purchase screen.

Payment and automatic renewal. Apple’s App Store or Google Play handles payment through your store account, and we do not receive payment details such as your card number. A subscription renews for the same period, and you are charged, unless you cancel at least 24 hours before the current period ends. If the price changes, you will be told in advance in the way the store requires.

Cancelling. You can cancel a subscription at any time in your store account’s subscription settings. After you cancel, you keep the membership until the end of the period you already paid for. Deleting the app or your app account does not cancel a subscription, so cancel it in the store first.

Refunds. Refunds follow Apple’s or Google’s policies, and you request them from that store. If the law where you live gives you a right to withdraw or to a refund, these terms do not limit that right.

When a membership ends. Members-only outfits, skins, screen looks and members-only features work only while your membership is active. When it ends, looks return to the default. A letter you handed over during your membership is still delivered on its set date after the membership ends.
Purchases by minors. If you are a minor, get permission from a parent or legal guardian before you buy.
after: We may change, pause or stop the app, any feature or the benefits of a membership, including letter limits and delivery timing. Letters in transit may be lost if the service stops. We will give notice in advance of a change that is worse for people with an active membership, or of ending the service, and we will refund where the law requires it. We will try to give notice of major changes in the app or on this page.

p: The app is provided “as is” and “as available”. To the extent the law allows, we make no warranties about the app, about other users or about the content of letters and replies, and we are not liable for indirect, incidental or consequential damages, or for loss of data. Nothing in these terms limits rights you have under laws that can’t be changed by contract.

You can stop using the app at any time and delete your account in Settings. We may suspend or end your access if you break these terms or if we need to in order to protect other users or comply with the law.

If you downloaded the app from Apple’s App Store, Apple’s Licensed Application End User License Agreement also applies, and these terms add to it. Apple and Google are not responsible for the app or its content. Purchases made in the app are also subject to the payment terms of the store you bought them from.

We may update these terms. When we do, we will change the effective date above, and if the change matters, we will tell you in the app. If you keep using the app after the change, you accept the new terms.
Questions about these terms: {emailLink}

privacy.title: Privacy Policy · Moss’s Club house
privacy.description: How Moss’s Club house handles your data: your account, letters and replies, approximate location, AI review and translation, notifications, and your choices.
privacy.intro: Moss’s Club house (the “app”) is made by Jongmin Lee, an independent developer at JML.Studio (“we”). This policy explains what information the app uses, why, who helps us process it and how long we keep it.
summary: Other users never see your name or email. They see your letter and an approximate city.

Letters and replies are sent to OpenAI for safety review and translation. OpenAI does not write them. A letter to your future self goes to no one else, and its text is sent to the external AI service only when you ask for a question, a summary card or a lookback.
Your approximate city comes from your network connection. The app doesn’t use GPS.
If you report being 19 or older, rewarded ads may be personalized or general. If you are 18 or younger, you can claim one spark a day by checking in.
Apple or Google handles payment for a paid membership. We do not receive payment details such as your card number.
You can delete your account and letters in the app at any time.

p: Account. When you sign in with Apple or Google, we receive an account identifier and your email address (Apple may give us a private relay address). We don’t store your name or profile photo from these providers. If you use Sign in with Apple, we also keep an encrypted Apple token so we can revoke your Apple sign-in when you delete your account.
Profile. Your app language, your time zone, your approximate city, the version of the terms you accepted and when you were last active.
Letters and replies. The text of letters and replies you write, their translations, review results, thank-you notes, and delivery details such as dates and which letters you were offered or chose.
Safety records. Reports you send, reports about your content, a copy of the reported content as the reporter saw it, the people you block, and account restrictions.
Notifications. If you allow notifications, your device’s push token and platform.

Promotion taps. When you open a link to one of our other apps, the app sends the app, link placement, platform and destination. The request uses your signed-in session. The daily aggregate table stores counts by those fields without account IDs or IP addresses.
Messages to us. If you email us, your email address and what you write.
Feedback. In-app feedback includes its type and text, language, platform, app version, receipt time and linked account.

Membership. When you buy or restore a membership, we receive and check the store’s proof of purchase: on the App Store a transaction signed by Apple, on Google Play a purchase token. From it we store the transaction identifier or purchase token, the product, when it expires and when we last checked it, with your account. Apple tells our server when a subscription renews, expires or is refunded. For an App Store purchase that was refunded or revoked, we keep only the transaction identifier and that time, apart from your account. When you buy, the app passes the store a random-looking identifier made from your account. It is not your account ID or email. Apple or Google handles payment details such as your card number, and we do not receive them. For a canceled Google Play lifetime purchase, we keep only a hash of the purchase token and the time we confirmed the cancellation, without an account link.

Focus keepsakes. The keepsakes you collect by finishing stretches with the focus timer. With your account we store which keepsakes you gathered and when each first came, and, for each focus place, the total focus time you finished there, the latest local date you finished a stretch there, the focus time you finished on that date, the number of days in a row, and, when needed to combine streaks across devices, which days you finished a stretch there in the seven days ending on that date. To check daily and streak keepsake eligibility across devices, we also store when you finished your latest counted stretch at each place and whether you had a membership when you started it. This lets you get your keepsakes back after reinstalling the app and see them on your other devices.

Shop rewards. We keep the age group you select (18 or younger, or 19 or older) and when you selected or last changed it. We do not ask for a birth date. We record daily reward dates and amounts, and for ad attempts, the account, session, ad unit, timing and a hashed Google transaction reference when credited.

On your device. Unsent drafts are stored on your device and are not submitted to the server until you send them. The focus timer’s record (time focused per day) and settings also stay on your device and are not sent to the server. Android backup rules exclude app data from automatic cloud backup and device transfer. On iOS, the folder holding drafts is marked as excluded from backup. This setting guides the OS and does not guarantee that backups or restores are prevented. Burning a draft does not erase copies in past backups.

Moss needs to know roughly where letters travel from and to. Our hosting provider estimates a city from your IP address. We round coordinates to about 10 km and store the approximate city separately from security records. Readers see only that city. The app does not request or use device location services.

For sign-in security, temporary rate-limit records contain IP-based keys. A scheduled cleanup removes records more than two days after their last request; delays in that job can delay removal. Session records do not store IP addresses or User-Agent values. This does not mean our hosting provider keeps no network or security logs.

We use this information to run the app: to sign you in, deliver letters between cities and time zones, translate letters, review content for safety, make a follow-up question, a summary card or a lookback for letters to your future self when you ask, show help resources when a letter suggests someone may need them, send notifications, handle reports and blocks, prevent abuse and rate limit requests, fix problems and answer your messages. We also use aggregate link counts to measure promotion of our own apps.

We use shop information to apply the age and daily limits, confirm ad completion, credit sparks and prevent abuse or duplicate rewards. We use membership information to confirm a membership purchase and provide its benefits, and to stop a refunded purchase from being used again. We use focus keepsakes to restore them after a reinstall and show them on your other devices.

Before a letter or reply is delivered, we send its text, its language and, for replies, the original letter as context, to OpenAI. OpenAI checks it against our letter rules and translates it. AI never writes or edits your letters. On newer app versions, we ask for permission on the screen where you accept the Terms of Use, either during setup or when you review the updated agreement. Your permission applies to later letters, replies and revisions. Older versions ask for permission each time you send.

Letters to your future self. These letters go to no one else, so they are not reviewed or translated. We send them to the external AI service only when you ask. If you ask for a question while writing, we send what you have written so far, the questions printed on that letter’s paper and the app language, and get one question back. If you ask for a summary card for a letter that has come back, we send that letter’s text and get back up to three passages chosen from it. If you ask for a lookback (My week, My month or My year), we send the text and writing dates of the letters that came back in that period and get back passages chosen from them. Letters that have not come back yet are not sent. A new letter shows one general question printed on the paper. It comes from a list built into the app and is picked by your device’s date, with no AI involved. Picking and printing it sends nothing anywhere. If you later ask for a question, the questions printed on the paper, including this one, are sent with that request. A question you ask for is made by the external AI service from what you have written so far. Until you send the letter, we do not store or log the text and question exchanged with the AI service while you write. When you send the letter, the questions printed on its paper are stored with it, shown again on the letter when it comes back, and deleted with the letter. We store summary cards and lookbacks with your letters, along with how many requests you made. Summary cards and lookbacks are made only from the letter’s own text, and the questions are never sent for them. If you never ask, your letters are not sent to the AI service. Your consent to this processing is recorded together with your acceptance of the terms when you tap “I agree” on first start or when reviewing updated terms.

To withdraw consent, delete your account in Settings > Delete account or email {emailLink}. Once you withdraw, you can no longer send letters, replies or encouragement letters, because they require processing by the AI service.

We send requests with OpenAI’s storage option turned off. According to OpenAI’s API policies, API data is not used to train their models by default, but OpenAI may keep it for a limited period to monitor abuse. See OpenAI’s Privacy Policy.
We use a small number of providers to run the app:
list: Cloudflare hosts our server and database and estimates your city from your IP address.
OpenAI reviews and translates letters and replies. For letters to your future self, it makes a question, a summary card or a lookback, and receives their text only when you ask for one.
Apple and Google provide sign-in. Apple Push Notification service (APNs) and Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) deliver notifications without letter text.

Google AdMob and its consent tool (UMP) may receive your IP address, an approximate location derived from it, app and device information (including available identifiers), ad views and interactions, and crash or performance data. Google uses this data to manage consent, serve and measure ads, and prevent fraud. We disable publisher first-party IDs. We send only an opaque attempt token as custom data to verify a reward. We do not send your app account ID, email or letter contents to ad providers. Google handles and retains SDK data under its Privacy Policy.

GitHub processes in-app feedback and letter or reply reports as issues in a private repository. Reports include the reason, content as the reporter saw it, content type, language, date and a report reference. We do not add account IDs or email addresses, though text may identify someone.

Apple (App Store) and Google (Google Play) process payment when you buy or restore a membership. They receive a random-looking identifier made from your account (not your account ID or email) and, for Google Play, the purchase token and product identifier. For a Google Play purchase, our server also asks Google when it confirms the purchase or checks the subscription again. You give your payment method and payment details to the store directly, and they do not pass through us. Letter content is not sent. Nothing is sent unless you buy a membership.
after: On iOS, when you first choose to watch an eligible ad, Apple may ask for App Tracking Transparency (ATT) permission. If you allow tracking and Google's regional consent permits personalization, we request personalized ads. If tracking is denied, we request general ads when Google permits ad requests. If ATT and any other required consent allow it, Google may use the iOS advertising identifier (IDFA) to measure ads or limit how often you see them, including for general ads. On Android, the Personalized ads switch in Settings is off by default. On Android, we block the advertising ID and advertising-related AdServices permissions. If you select personalized ads, the request is subject to Google’s rules and the data available. Google may still serve general ads. When personalization is not allowed, we request general ads if Google’s consent tool permits requests. If it does not permit requests, we do not request ads.
These providers may process information in the United States and other countries. They handle it under their own terms and privacy policies.

p: We keep your account and letters while your account exists. A letter travels for at most 14 days. If nobody replies, it comes back to you. You can burn a returned letter and its reply, which deletes their text, translations and review data and leaves only a minimal record that the letter existed. Letters to your future self (their text, the questions printed on the paper, when sent, the return day, when read, the summary card and the passages chosen for lookbacks) are kept until you delete the letter or your account. When you delete a letter, its text, its printed questions, its summary card and the lookback passages chosen from it are removed; a random identifier and the day it was sent stay until you delete your account, so the same letter is not sent twice. We keep the kind and period of each lookback made until you delete your account, and a scheduled job deletes the counts of requests for questions, summary cards and lookbacks after 7 days.

When you delete your account, we delete the account, sessions, your letters and replies you wrote. We revoke the Apple sign-in tokens available to us and guide you if you need to remove Apple access manually. We remove linked private GitHub feedback asynchronously within 7 days; deletion is complete only after that cleanup. To review safety issues, we retain reports you filed or received, including their reason, reported content and handling status, without user IDs for up to 90 days, then delete them. The text may still identify someone. Membership information (product, transaction identifier or purchase token, expiry) and focus keepsakes are kept until you delete your account and are deleted with it. The transaction identifier and time of a refunded or revoked App Store purchase are kept for 3 years without account information, including after you delete your account, to stop a refunded purchase from being used again. For a canceled Google Play lifetime purchase, the hash of the purchase token and the cancellation confirmation time are kept for 3 years from the latest confirmation, also without account information and after account deletion. Cloudflare D1 recovery history may retain deleted data for up to 30 days, depending on the plan. Other provider records follow their own retention rules.

After delivery, we clear feedback text from our Cloudflare D1 database. We delete the raw feedback issue and related copies no later than 90 days after it is closed or 180 days after receipt, whichever comes first. Unresolved feedback is deleted within 180 days of receipt.

We delete GitHub report issues and related copies by the earliest of 180 days after receipt, 90 days after the issue is closed or the report is resolved by an administrator, or 90 days after account deletion. This deadline applies to GitHub copies; the safety records described above follow their own retention period.

After a deletion request is completed, we keep verification evidence and request metadata until the earlier of 90 days after completion or 180 days after receipt. For unfinished requests, we retain the minimum needed to complete the work.

Your ad choice is stored on this device for your account. We keep the current age group, when it was set, and awarded reward records until account deletion. A scheduled cleanup removes ad attempt records after one day has passed since the applicable daily reward window closed; account deletion also removes them. Google’s own data follows its retention rules.
You can delete your account in Settings > Delete account. You can turn notifications off in your device settings. You can block anyone who writes to you.

The app has no way to change a saved age group. To correct it, ask as described in section 7. On Android, you can turn personalized ads on or off in the app’s Settings. When personalization is not permitted, general ads may be requested. Where available, Ad privacy choices manages Google’s regional consent separately. On iOS, you can change the separate ATT permission in the device’s Settings > Privacy & Security > Tracking. You can exchange letters without watching ads.

Depending on where you live, you may have the right to access, correct, delete or export your information, or to object to or restrict how we use it. To make a request, email {emailLink}. You can also complain to your local data protection authority.
The app is not intended for children under {age}. If you believe a child under that age is using the app, contact us and we will delete the account.
We do not request ads or load ad consent forms for accounts that report being 18 or younger.

Data is sent over HTTPS, access to our systems is limited, and our logs record error codes, not letter text or account IDs. No service can be perfectly secure, so please don’t put identifying information in your letters.

This website, including the page where this policy is published, uses Google Analytics 4 to understand visits. Google may receive browser and device information, an approximate location from your IP address, the pages you view and cookies or similar identifiers, under Google’s Privacy Policy. The app itself does not use Google Analytics.
If we change this policy, we will update the effective date above. If the change matters, we will tell you in the app before it takes effect.
Jongmin Lee, JML.Studio: {emailLink}
